public_rationale: He says that, in reality, at most a few hundred megawatts of usable AI capacity comes online each quarter. Epoch AI tracks AI data centers using satellite imagery and permits, independently of company claims. For January to March 2026, the last full quarter before the post, its estimates show three sites alone adding about 766 MW of operational IT power: Amazon's New Carlisle campus about 284 MW, Meta's Prometheus about 292 MW, and DayOne Nusajaya in Malaysia about 190 MW. Several smaller sites added more in the same quarter, and Epoch says its database covers less than half of global AI compute. Epoch's figures carry error bands (80% within a factor of 1.4) and some dates are inferred. But even a discount of that size leaves three sites above a few hundred megawatts in one quarter. Facility power, which includes cooling, is higher still.
limitations: Epoch's figures are modeled estimates, and some operational dates are inferred from typical build times.
"A few hundred megawatts" has no exact ceiling; about 500 MW was used as the plain upper bound.
Only one quarter is tested; he said "every quarter".

statement.excerpt: While it sounds a little wild, I think in reality only a few hundred megawatts — if that — of actual, usable AI compute capacity is being spun up every quarter.
statement.document_title: Where Are All The Data Centers?

from_speaker: "only a few hundred megawatts — if that"
our_interpretation: "I think" signals belief, but the claim is a firm figure: industry-wide, no more than a few hundred megawatts of usable AI capacity comes online per quarter.
Scope is the whole AI industry worldwide, since no company or region is named.
Present tense with no named period: tested against the most recent full quarter before the 12 May 2026 post, January to March 2026.
"Usable" means capacity that is operational (energized, with compute running), not merely built or contracted. Independent measurement is preferred over company claims, which he disputes.
"A few hundred megawatts, if that" is read as roughly 500 MW or less per quarter.
criteria.support_condition: Independent measurement showing that operational AI data center capacity worldwide rose by about 500 MW or less in January to March 2026.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Independent measurement showing that operational AI capacity added in January to March 2026 clearly exceeded a few hundred megawatts, for example well over 500 MW of IT power across a subset of sites.

evidence.excerpt: We expect that 80% of the time, a given IT power capacity estimate is accurate within a factor of 1.4x. For compute capacity, this factor increases to 1.5x, and for cost, the factor is 1.6x. As for the timelines, we expect that 80% of the time, our estimated date is within 6 months of the actual date.
evidence.locator: FAQ: How confident are you in the data?
evidence.explanation: Epoch's capacities and dates are estimates with real error bands, and some operational dates are inferred from typical build times. Even if capacity is cut by a factor of 1.4, three sites still exceed about 500 MW. Timing errors could move some of it into adjacent quarters.
